headline: OROSUR DRILLS 61m AT 0.93 G/T GOLD FROM SURFACE AT EL CEDRO — FIRST HOLE OPEN TO 500m DEPTH IN COLOMBIA'S MID-CAUCA BELT
snippet: Orosur Mining Inc (TSXV: OMI) announced September 15 that its maiden drill hole CED001 at the El Cedro target within the Anzá Project in Colombia's Mid-Cauca gold belt returned 61.35 metres averaging 0.93 g/t Au from surface, including a higher-grade interval of 42.15 metres at 1.02 g/t Au. The hole is part of a first-ever systematic drill program across a 530km² project area and is planned to continue to 500 metres depth, with the company noting increasing vein density below 130 metres and pending assays suggesting potential for higher-grade cores at depth.

headline: OREZONE MAPS 14-YEAR, 1.63MOZ LIFE-OF-MINE PLAN AT CASA BERARDI — QUEBEC GOLD MINE DRILLING UP TO 100,000m/YEAR
snippet: Orezone Gold Corporation (TSX/ASX: ORE) published September 15 an updated Life-of-Mine plan for its Casa Berardi gold mine in Quebec projecting 14 continuous years of operations from 2027 through 2040 and total production of 1,630,000 ounces via combined underground and open-pit mining. Orezone acquired the operation from Hecla Mining in March 2026 for approximately $352 million and has since reinitiated exploration, ramping to 100,000 metres per year of drilling to define the Principal and WMCP open-pit potential that underpins up to $231 million of contingent milestone payments.

headline: STANMORE BUYS EXXARO'S 724Mt MORANBAH SOUTH COAL BLOCK FOR $105M — BOWEN BASIN CONSOLIDATION ACCELERATES
snippet: Stanmore Resources (ASX: SMR) announced September 14 it has agreed to acquire 100% of the Moranbah South premium hard coking coal tenements in Queensland's Bowen Basin from Exxaro Resources for US$105 million, conditional on Exxaro first obtaining full ownership from Anglo American via a pre-emptive rights exercise. The project holds 724 million tonnes of measured and indicated resources in the Goonyella Middle Seam and is adjacent to Stanmore's existing Eagle Downs and Isaac Plains Complex operations, with completion targeted before the end of Q4 2026 pending FIRB and ACCC approvals.

headline: LINQ DRILLS 113m AT 0.71% CUEQ AT GILMORE — MACQUARIE ARC PORPHYRY CONFIRMS BULK-TONNAGE COPPER-GOLD SCALE
snippet: LinQ Minerals (ASX: LNQ) reported September 15 phase one maiden drilling results at the Gilmore Gold-Copper Project in the Macquarie Arc, New South Wales, with a highlight hole returning 113 metres at 0.71% copper equivalent from 33 metres including 72 metres at 0.95% CuEq and a 4-metre high-grade interval at 5.3% CuEq; a second hole delivered 193 metres at 0.45% CuEq from 49 metres. Results from the Monza Gold-Copper prospect within Gilmore's Central Zone confirm bulk-tonnage porphyry-style mineralisation in one of Australia's most prolific copper-gold belts.

headline: NORD PRECIOUS METALS UPGRADES GOWGANDA TO 2.814MOZ SILVER AT 47.4 G/T — T ENGINEERING SIGNED FOR 2027 TAILINGS REPROCESSING
snippet: Nord Precious Metals Mining Inc. (TSXV: NTH) reported September 15 an updated Indicated Mineral Resource Estimate for its Gowganda Silver Tailings Project in Ontario of 1.845 million tonnes grading 47.4 g/t silver, containing 2.814 million ounces. Canadian engineering firm T Engineering has been engaged to conduct pilot-scale testing and optimize reprocessing parameters ahead of a targeted 2027 production start, positioning Gowganda as a lower-capital-intensity path to silver output from surface historical tailings at the company's Gowganda-Castle district in northern Ontario.

headline: COPPER FINDS FOOTING NEAR $14,000 AS LME WAREHOUSE DELIVERIES DRAIN THE TARIFF-SQUEEZE PREMIUM
snippet: Copper steadied near US$14,000 per tonne on September 15 as fresh deliveries of refined metal to LME exchange-tracked warehouses signalled an easing of the supply squeeze that drove the metal to a record US$14,533 earlier this month, with traders who had diverted supplies to the US ahead of anticipated tariffs now returning inventories to international markets. The LME three-month contract posted little change after its lowest close in four weeks; analysts note the metal still trades 35% above year-ago levels, with ongoing production declines at Codelco and Freeport-McMoRan providing structural support.

headline: URANIUM TERM PRICE TOPS $96.50, CLEARING 2007 RECORD — U.S. UTILITIES LEAVE 186 MILLION POUNDS UNCOVERED THROUGH 2035
snippet: Crux Investor analysis confirms uranium's long-term contract price closed August 2026 at US$96.50 per pound — the first time it has exceeded its 2007 all-time peak and an 18-year high driven by producer inventory exhaustion rather than a new wave of utility buying. U.S. utilities hold contracted deliveries of 174 million pounds against requirements of 360 million pounds for 2026-2035, leaving 186 million pounds (roughly 52% of anticipated needs) entirely uncovered, while Kazatomprom's latest quota cut lowered 2026 nominal capacity by 8 million pounds to approximately 77 million pounds annually; Bank of America cites this gap as the basis for a US$130/lb price target.

headline: GOLDSEEK MAPS BUY ZONES FOR MINERS AFTER CPI — WHERE TO ACCUMULATE GOLD EQUITIES IN THE PRE-FOMC SELLOFF
snippet: GoldSeek's September 13 analysis argues that the latest CPI release — headline inflation at 3.4% with core cooling to 2.4% despite hotter producer prices at 5.4% — has created a textbook buy zone for gold mining equities, with producers now trading at valuations that have historically preceded multi-month rallies following the first rate hike in a tightening cycle. The piece identifies specific technical accumulation zones for GDX and individual producers that have held through prior FOMC-driven selloffs, framing the current discount as an entry window for investors who accept the hike is fully priced and are positioning for the post-decision recovery.

headline: SILVER TO $58 BY SEPT 30? INDUSTRY SPREAD MAKES THE SPEC-LENGTH UNWIND CASE WITH FOMC 92% PRICED
snippet: The Industry Spread's pre-FOMC analysis argues that silver's speculative long positioning — rebuilt to the 73rd percentile of the past 60 weeks into a falling market — sets up a disorderly unwind if the Fed's September 16 statement turns hawkish, with a base case of $58.00/oz by September 30, a bear case at $55.30, and a bull case at $70.30. The mechanism: net longs were still being added into the August 28 high at $68 discounting a rate cut that Wednesday's hike removes; with 92.5% of the hike already priced, the tail risk lies in the post-decision forward guidance, not the decision itself.

headline: SAXO COT: GOLD LONGS AT A 60-WEEK LOW WHILE SILVER CROWDS TO THE 73RD PERCENTILE — A DIVERGENCE THAT MATTERS PRE-FOMC
snippet: Saxo Bank's September 14 CFTC positioning update for the week ending September 8 reveals a striking divergence between gold and silver ahead of Wednesday's FOMC decision: speculative net longs in gold futures fell to just the 20th percentile of the past 60 weekly readings as long liquidation and fresh shorts compressed the position, while silver's speculative net longs sit at the 73rd percentile — rebuilt entirely on the long side with gross short positions staying comparatively thin throughout the decline. The data suggest gold is substantially less vulnerable to a hike-driven positioning unwind than silver, complicating the typical narrative that both metals fall together on a hawkish Fed.
